newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO CETES RATE UP ON PROFIT-TAKING.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO CETES RATE UP ON PROFIT-TAKING.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 60 basis points in early trade on Thursday.
Dealers said rates rose on profit-taking after a sharp drop the day before under pressure from players with heavy liquidity positions.
"Some players prefer to hang onto their money and buy after rates have risen a little," a trader said.
Dealers said rates could ease down as the session progressed due to expectations the central bank would announce mild inflation data later in the day.
The latest Reuters survey of forecasts by 14 Mexico City financial houses MEX22 showed they predicted the Consumer Price Index would rise by 0.88 percent for July, compared with 0.89 percent in June.
Overnight rates on bank paper were meanwhile trading down 15 basis points at 18.90 percent.
Liquidity of 1.497 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation, in addition to 500 million pesos in cash.
Dealers said an overplacement of 1.497 billion pesos at this week's central bank auction would reduce market liquidity.
